title: Are Saints ‘to be adored’? Strict latria—no; broader human cult—yes
source_text: IX. Similiter quum quaeritur an Sancti sint adorandi, & an cultus Sanctis debitus adoratio dici debeat, annon: respondent eodem modo adorationem alias stricte sumi pro cultu Latriae, qui soli Deo convenit; & hoc sensu Sanctos non esse adorandos: alias vero largius accipi, & extendi ad cultum humanum, & qui debetur creaturis, & latiori hac significatione Sanctos adorari debere, & eorum cultum dici posse adorationem.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise when it is asked whether the Saints are to be adored, and whether the cult owed to the Saints ought to be called adoration, or not: they answer in the same way that adoration is sometimes taken strictly for the cult of Latria, which befits God alone; and in this sense the Saints are not to be adored: but otherwise it is taken more largely, and extended to human cult, and that which is owed to creatures, and in this broader signification the Saints ought to be adored, and their cult can be called adoration.
pass_b_english: ‘Adoration’ strict = latria for God alone—Saints out.
‘Adoration’ broad = creaturely honor—Saints in, and their cult may wear the name.

choices.why: Keep the contested verb; sense splits on scope.
